contracts.topic: Physical mesh ownership and node copy
contracts.statement: MeshAdaptive owns SubMesh objects; SubMesh owns nodes/elements. SetNoh copies ID, position and curvature state into an independent node, clearing foreign element observers. AddNoh transfers unique ownership and preserves identity; SetElement consumes an exclusive raw argument before any vector allocation by delegating to the owning AddElement entry point. Success preserves ordered identity and null slots; failure destroys the argument and preserves existing owned slots. MeshAdaptive raw SubMesh insertions consume exclusive ownership on entry, before vector growth or position validation. Growth failure leaves existing slots unchanged and destroys the argument; negative positions leave the container unchanged and destroy the consumed argument. Success preserves identity/order and sparse null slots, replacing and destroying any old item. SubMesh destruction releases elements before nodes. Move assignment explicitly retires old elements before replacing node owners; incoming owner addresses/order and patch observer value survive. Self-move preserves the graph.
contracts.limits: The source of SetNoh remains caller-owned. Only this boundary and local reconstruction/move/replacement are instrumented; general NodeAdaptive value copies and full mesh lifecycles remain separate. MeshAdaptive adoption requires uniquely owned actual SubMesh objects, nonthrowing destructors and no duplicate/re-adopted aliases; SubMesh is not polymorphically deletable. Failure consumes the argument; no reuse of that pointer is valid. Existing graph identity, node adjacency and analytic triangle area, allocation-denied growth, negative/null/nonallocating paths and container move/removal are qualified by isolated actual-unit probes. Successful replacement/removal invalidates foreign observers; caller rebinding is not automatic. Other constructors, full-process/parallel memory and logical rejection remain separate. Element adoption qualification covers actual triangles with live exclusively owned nodes, empty/populated/null/spare-storage layouts, normal identity/area/coordinates/IDs/UV/adjacency and allocation-free terminal owner unwinding. Constructors have already registered adjacency before entry. TriangleAdaptive destruction now removes its registrations from live current vertex nodes. The current terminal adoption probe requires exact live prefix adjacency before rethrow; a dedicated current-entry paired probe additionally qualifies safe prior traversal and fresh-argument adoption after denied raw/owning growth in empty/populated containers. A consumed failed argument is never reused; this does not add production CLI retry or general graph rollback. Constructor-before-entry registration qualification is limited to C05; SubMesh move/destruction qualification covers empty, populated, node-only, repeated-vertex and null-slot graphs with nonthrowing counted actual triangle subclasses. Elements must borrow local nodes or independently live external nodes; a graph borrowing nodes owned by the replaced destination is invalid. No foreign Patch observer is rebound. Eight measured move/destruction paths perform zero allocations, including teardown. Arbitrary element subclasses and cross-owner lifetime arrangements remain unqualified.

contracts.statement: TriangleAdaptive borrows three NodeAdaptive pointers, registers itself in each adjacency and caches normal, area and angles. NodeAdaptive adjacency is an observer list. Parameterized TriangleAdaptive construction registers in original vertex order and removes every matching fresh-this observer on C++ construction failure before rethrowing. NodeAdaptive::RemoveElementObserver removes pointer entries without deleting elements or allocating. Existing list nodes, order, null markers and scalar state are preserved, including repeated vertex nodes. TriangleAdaptive has stable address identity: copy/move construction and assignment are explicitly deleted. ReplaceNode selects the first matching vertex in n1/n2/n3 order. Same/absent vertices are no-ops; a matched replacement requires live non-null nodes and an existing registration. MoveElementObserverTo transfers the first matching physical list node to the destination tail using splice, without allocation or element deletion; only then is the vertex pointer committed. Other entries, list-node identities, null markers, node state, triangle ID/UV and cached geometry are unchanged. Completed TriangleAdaptive destruction removes matching this observers from each non-null current vertex without allocating or deleting nodes/elements. Repeated vertices are idempotent; the default all-null object is safe. Cleanup applies through ElementAdaptive virtual deletion and base destruction after a derived constructor throws.
contracts.limits: General NodeAdaptive value copies retain foreign observer lists; SubMesh::SetNoh explicitly clears them. Borrowed vertex nodes and their valid lists must outlive the complete triangle, including destruction. Other foreign copied lists are not scanned. Constructor failure rollback remains qualified for a fresh address, live non-null nodes and all observed allocation ordinals. Completed destruction qualification covers distinct/reversed/repeated vertices, default emptiness, a controlled derived constructor failure, equivalent/merged first-match replacement, exact unrelated list-node/null/order/scalar restoration, safe parent traversal and fresh component construction. Eight measured completed destruction paths allocate nothing; default/derived construction setup is outside that claim. Four raw/owning empty/populated positive vector-growth denials restore the prior live graph before safe traversal and fresh-argument adoption outside the hook. No production CLI retry, consumed-object reuse, metadata/error/history/ID rollback or cache refresh is introduced. Geometry validity after coordinate-changing replacement remains unqualified. Arbitrary protected vertex mutation/subclasses, externally expired nodes, unobserved external/conditional callers, general whole-process/parallel/LSan/UBSan memory and estimator root ownership remain separate. SubMesh element-before-node destruction/move ordering remains qualified in C04.

contracts.statement: Patch stores a non-owning current SubMesh pointer and SubMesh stores a non-owning Patch pointer. PatchCoons borrows Geometry-owned curves. Estimator construction delegates to BuildInitialEstimateSubMesh and returns one exclusive physical mesh owner; the raw InitialMeshEstimate compatibility wrapper releases that owner to its caller without a hidden MeshAdaptive. Only completed construction publishes the patch observer. Unpublished copied source nodes and pending triangles have local owners; the first successful curve insertion transfers a sample to the existing collective lifetime. Positive degrees use a nonfloating iteration ceiling while preserving the original floating endpoint test and repeated additions. Nonpositive degrees are rejected before patch access. CalculateNumbersTriangle delegates to CountEstimateTriangles. Its temporary SubMesh has one unique owner; a nonallocating scope restores the previous patch observer and deletes fresh samples published only into its four initially empty curve lists. Preexisting point and parameter list nodes, borrowed samples and their element observers survive. Shared corner/repeated-curve aliases are cleared before each owned sample is deleted once. CalculateErroEstimative privately owns its temporary GeneratorAdaptive with unique_ptr through normal return and exception propagation; the mesh and timer remain borrowed. The historical strict minor_degree_ update and inclusive error stopping threshold are preserved; minor_error_ is not updated. CalculateAreaTriangleMedio gives its temporary MeshAdaptive automatic lifetime and uses the same selective EstimateMeshScope as counting. Each construction remains owned until insertion consumes it; restoration and fresh-sample cleanup run before physical mesh destruction. Error evaluation precedes the degree cap, replacement construction precedes removal, and the final selected-degree reconstruction and first-triangle area publication remain in their original order.
contracts.limits: Replacing a submesh invalidates old observers; rollback must rebind every patch before the next adaptation. Qualification covers planar/bilinear degree 1/2/4 and four initialization masks with unchanged grid loops, UV evaluation order and historical center IDs. The bounded serial error-evaluator caller qualification uses actual class/dependency units with exact extracted generator constructor/ErrorGlobal bodies; full historical generator/estimator translation units, parallel and full-process memory remain unqualified. Rebind patch before destroying the returned mesh; nonpositive degree guards cover 0/-1/INT_MIN; arbitrary patches and extreme complete meshes are unqualified. Scalar sampling compatibility covers 520 positive degrees independently of full mesh validity. Counting requires fixed topology, four live non-null curves and the actual factory publication semantics: initially nonempty lists are borrowed and unchanged; initially empty lists receive only fresh uniquely deletable samples. No concurrent access or arbitrary patch callback publication. Exact lifetime qualification covers plane/bilinear degree 1/2/4 with seven graph layouts and all observed allocation ordinals; repeated incidences and independent parameter-list fixtures are lifetime guards, not complete geometric validity. Evaluator scratch and CLI retry remain outside scope. Required area lifetime qualification separates controlled orchestration from actual-error integration. The controlled error-member test executable is separate from actual-error integration; no production callback abstraction is introduced. Selected-zero rejection and exception-visible minor_degree_ updates remain unchanged. Degree-5 execution only exercises the historical cap/lifetime path, not general non-power-of-two geometric validity. Mesh, sample and patch observers require the fixed topology and publication rules above.

contracts.statement: Geometry reuses matching four-control Bezier curves in direct or reverse direction. CurveAdaptive does not delete its sampled points; its point and patch lists are observers. SetPoints and UpdateParameters each commit their prepared by-value list by swap; allocation failure preserves that live list and its element nodes. Successful replacement preserves ordered pointer/value results and invalidates old list-element observers without deleting borrowed points or patches. Initialized non-null pointer-taking parametric, Bezier and Hermite copies preserve parameter values/order in independent list nodes alongside the same borrowed sampled points and patches. CloneCurveForPatch returns a pending unique owner through target-incidence insertion. The synchronization-disabled consumer prepares all clones per original curve before batch publication and nonallocating incidence commit; failure preserves the failing curve and any already committed prefix, and whole-operation retry is supported within the qualified graph fixtures. The target-count rebuild helper prepares unique replacement nodes and both the supplied point list and curve parameter list before nonallocating paired swaps and old-interior deletion. Failure preserves both lists, element nodes and old samples; consumed manager IDs remain consumed and retry uses the subsequent IDs. Successful growth preserves uniform parameter formulas and endpoint objects; shrinking preserves rounded index selection and original paired values. The identical construction tails of both serial Adapter methods delegate to BuildCurveSamples. New endpoint/interior nodes, parameters, cache changes and the return list are prepared under exclusive pending ownership. Commit occurs only after return construction succeeds: prepared map nodes merge without allocating, existing cache entry nodes remain stable, parameters swap and new owners release. Failure preserves borrowed samples, curve point observers, parameter list nodes and cache nodes/values; consumed IDs remain consumed. Endpoint scalar/adjacency copy, cached reuse and alias-overwrite policies are preserved. Generator delegates its serial curve/surface/optional-rebuild publication sequence to RefineCurveSamples. A collective RAII transaction prepares equivalent working lists and a cache-value snapshot before parking original point/parameter list nodes. Returned sample lists enter ownership through nonthrowing move assignment before point-observer copies. Failure removes new cache keys, restores existing values in place, deduplicates and reclaims new nonborrowed samples, and restores the original point/parameter nodes. Success deletes superseded first-pass interiors without allocating and transfers final samples to the existing collective graph lifetime. IDs consumed before failure remain consumed; retry uses the subsequent sequence. The serial AdaptCurve scope now uses CurveSampleGraphTransaction across preparation, policy calculations and the complete curve loop. All equivalent working point/parameter lists and the deduplicated initial sample inventory are prepared before original list nodes are parked. Initial samples remain alive across committed per-curve prefixes. Failure clears the operation-local cache, deletes every newly published sample once without allocating, and restores every original point/parameter list node and shared sample object. Success retires the collectively owned initial samples once after the complete loop, leaving final samples under the existing caller graph lifetime. Consumed IDs are not rewound. Serial Generator gives the currently published sample graph one CurveSampleLifetime scope owner before initialization. Normal explicit release and exceptional destruction clear every shared alias before deleting each object once without allocating. Inner sample graph guards unwind before the outer lifetime owner; fatal CLI exceptions do not introduce metadata recovery or retry. Serial InitialMesh delegates to BuildInitialSubMesh, which owns its pending SubMesh, unpublished samples, center temporary and triangles. The first successful curve insertion transfers a sample to the existing collective owner; element insertion consumes a unique owner. Only complete construction publishes the patch observer and returns an owned mesh. The raw compatibility wrapper releases to its valid presized caller.

contracts.statement: Default AdvancingFront allocates Boundary/Quadtree. Quadtree owns generated template vertices, edges and faces until an allocation-free ordered splice transfers them to front owner lists. It destroys any untransferred template payload on failure or abandonment before deleting its root/boundary. Default front construction guards Boundary until Quadtree construction completes; failure before adoption leaves no retained boundary. TemplateStorage owns unregistered template buffers/objects and releases only successfully registered prefixes to Quadtree. Outer creation uses local vertex/edge guards until registration. Initial root extents stay locally owned until root construction succeeds. Midpoint buffers and all five vertices remain locally owned until complete construction; successful allocation and subdivision order is unchanged.
contracts.limits: Getters return borrowed pointer views; template owner getters are empty after transfer. External-pointer constructor/setter replacement, mate-root sharing, full-process cleanup remain unqualified. After a template creation exception, the tree is qualified for destruction only; observer consumption and same-tree retry are not supported by this slice. Prepared fixture covers types 1 and 4, not all patterns. Root-only generation, one uniform subdivision, edge/old-face generation and prepared neighbor refinement are allocation-failure destruction controls; failed trees must not be queried or retried.

contracts.statement: Edge/Face destructors retain legacy endpoint ownership outside shared containers. Boundary, Quadtree and front cleanup call DetachVertices without allocating; Face detachment releases a midpoint alias to an endpoint while preserving distinct cache ownership. Edge/Face setVertices prepare owned caches before committing endpoints; allocation failure preserves live state. Face cache replacement preserves an old endpoint-alias midpoint as borrowed. Boundary registration guards temporary vertices/edges and commits IDs/contour state only after owner nodes succeed, rolling back edge observers on failure. Face::quality owns temporary centers and detaches its borrowed-endpoint edge on unwind. Public subdivision queries require an attached quadtree and throw std::logic_error when it is missing; owned-cell numerical criteria remain unchanged. Edge::angle(Vertex*, Vertex*) also detaches its temporary borrowed endpoints on every exit, including allocation failure during cache construction/reset or copied adjacency. Edge::makeParamMid prepares an owned replacement and normalized length before committing either; allocation failure preserves the old cache identity/geometry and edge state. Successful replacement delays old-cache destruction until preparation completes and invalidates old cache observers.
contracts.limits: Conditional detachment remains explicit; normal, partial, failed/exceptional post-template exits and selected transfer-allocation failures are isolated controls, not universal observer ownership or arbitrary exception safety. New setter endpoints must not alias a distinct cache owned by that object. Generic individual setters, parametric midpoint replacement and template/Boundary registration failures are not covered by the primitive slice. Registration controls use a null-curve fixture and a quadtree prepared through the real front generate/refine sequence; they do not qualify curve-internal failures, arbitrary setters or all helper paths. Angle-helper qualification covers four endpoint-match branches and the nonadjacent branch with empty/populated caller adjacency; it does not qualify every helper or curve operation. Parametric replacement controls cover four sides in both incidence directions, two interior fallbacks and a null-curve no-op. Curve evaluation scratch remains mutable. Zero observed allocations in the measured polynomial evaluation/integration/bisection do not establish curve-internal allocation-failure coverage; other curve mutation, initialization and shared samples remain unqualified.
